table.purpose: Rows keyed by a composite-style ID (e.g. GW386_86) that pairs a parent code (GW386) with a sub-index; each row is a sub-item/variant of a parent entity tracked in t04, with a short category/status tag. Exact domain is unresolved from the data alone.

col_001.name: sub_item_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Composite identifier formed as '<parent_code>_<sub_index>' (e.g. GW386_86); the prefix matches col_002, which references t04. Each value is unique across 12,333 rows.

col_002.name: parent_code
col_002.description: Parent/group code (e.g. GW386) extracted from the prefix of col_001; references t04.col_001. 444 distinct parents, each with multiple sub-items. The 'GW' prefix and numbering scheme's real-world meaning is unresolved.

table.purpose: Unresolved: rows are keyed by composite codes like 'GW386_69_81' that pair a GW identifier (col_002) with two numeric parts, possibly coordinates, positions, or version/sequence numbers. The table likely enumerates sub-items (e.g., positions, segments, or measurements) belonging to each GW entity, but the domain cannot be determined from the data alone.

col_001.name: item_id
col_001.description: Primary key. Composite code formed as '<GW id>_<num1>_<num2>', where the GW id matches col_002. The two numeric suffixes (e.g., 69_81, 03_12) are unresolved: they could be coordinates, indices, or version numbers. Uniquely identifies each row.

col_002.name: gw_id
col_002.description: Group/entity code (e.g., GW386) shared by many rows; the prefix of col_001. References t04.col_001, so t04 likely holds one row per GW entity and this table its sub-items.

table.name: well_pair_link
table.purpose: Link/junction table pairing two entities (likely wells or stations coded GW###_#) from t01; each row represents an ordered pair, with col_003 being the composite pair identifier that references the pair table t02. The GW prefix and structure suggest groundwater wells, but this is inferred from code format only.

col_001.name: first_entity_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the first member of the pair; references t01.col_001 (many-to-one). Format GW###_#, e.g. GW369_66. Same value set as col_002, so it is one of the two paired entities.

col_002.name: second_entity_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the second member of the pair; references t01.col_001 (many-to-one). Always shares the GW### prefix with col_001 in the same row, so pairs are formed within the same group/site (e.g. GW369_66 with GW369_60).

col_003.name: pair_id
col_003.description: Composite identifier of the pair, formed by concatenating col_001 and col_002 (e.g. GW369_66 + GW369_60 -> GW369_66_60). References t02.col_001 (many-to-one), the table of pairs.

table.purpose: Unresolved: a table of 343 entities identified by codes like 'GW333' (possibly objects in a catalog, e.g. galaxies or similar, given the GW-style identifiers), each carrying a binary sign flag. The exact domain cannot be determined from the data alone. It is referenced by t01 and t02, suggesting it acts as a lookup/master list of these entities.

col_001.name: entity_code
col_001.description: Primary key: unique code identifying each row's entity, formatted 'GW' followed by a number (e.g. GW333, GW672). Referenced by t01.col_002 and t02.col_002, so it serves as the master identifier that other tables link to. The 'GW' prefix suggests a catalog naming scheme, but the exact entity type is unresolved.
